The disappearing peaks are most likely artifacts of PFA-only fixation. Formaldehyde crosslinking is relatively slow, allowing soluble proteins (including transcription factors like IKAROS) to redistribute and bind non-specifically to highly accessible, open chromatin regions before becoming fully crosslinked. This generates false-positive "phantom peaks" at active promoters and enhancers. The addition of DSG (a faster-acting protein–protein crosslinker) prior to formaldehyde fixation stabilizes the native protein complexes and prevents this redistribution, eliminating these artifactual peaks. 

Furthermore, standard ChIP-seq quality control, alignment, and peak-calling pipelines filter out reads mapping to repetitive regions (due to low mappability), so peaks called from standard analysis are overwhelmingly located in unique, mappable regions—primarily active regulatory elements—not in repeats or random genomic locations. 

Answer: D
